newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland welcomes NATO enlargement schedule.
newsitem.headline: Poland welcomes NATO enlargement schedule.

text.p: Poland welcomed NATO's decision on Tuesday to hold a summit next year at which it will invite some of its former communist foes from eastern Europe to join the alliance.
"Poland is undoubtedly satisfied. We treat this as a very serious step moving us closer (to NATO)," foreign ministry spokesman Pawel Dobrowolski said.
NATO's 16 foreign ministers decided in Brussels that the enlargement summit would be held next July 8 and 9 in Madrid, despite Russia's opposition to the pact's expansion.
Russia says its security would be threatened if the pact's military infrastructure moved closer to its borders.
Poland, along with the Czech Republic and Hungary, is widely expected to be among the first former Warsaw Pact members to begin accession talks.

Dobrowolski said that Poland accepted the United States' declaration on Tuesday, seen as aimed at appeasing Moscow, that there were no plans or need to station nuclear weapons on the territory of new members.
"The Polish side stresses it is good that if, looking at the issue from a global perspective, there there is no such need (to station nuclear weapons)," he said.
But he said that nuclear arms should be a subject in the accession negotiations with candidate countries.
